Cross-cohort or cross-contrast effect-size concordance scatter plot

Source: R/plot_omics_extra.R
plot_concordance.Rd

Plots per-protein effect sizes from two cohorts, platforms, or contrasts against each other, annotates Pearson r, Spearman rho, and sign-concordance percentage, and optionally labels the top concordant or discordant proteins.

Usage

plot_concordance(
  data,
  x_col,
  y_col,
  assay_col = "Assay",
  max_labels = 10,
  show_stats = TRUE,
  show_smooth = TRUE,
  identity_line = FALSE,
  colors = c(Same = "#009E73", Opposite = "#D55E00"),
  xlab = x_col,
  ylab = y_col,
  title = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data.frame with one row per shared protein.

x_col, y_col

Names of the two numeric effect-size columns.

assay_col

Optional protein label column name (default `"Assay"`).

max_labels

Number of top extreme proteins (by `|x| + |y|`) to label when `assay_col` is present (default `10`; `0` disables).

show_stats

Logical; annotate Pearson r, Spearman rho, and in the subtitle (default `TRUE`).

show_smooth

Logical; overlay a linear regression line with 95 (default `TRUE`).

identity_line

Logical; draw the `y = x` dashed diagonal (default `FALSE`).

colors

Named vector of length 2 for `"Same"` and `"Opposite"` sign quadrants.

xlab, ylab

Axis labels (default `x_col`, `y_col`).

title

Optional plot title.

Value

A `ggplot` object.

Examples

set.seed(42)
df <- data.frame(
  Assay = paste0("P", 1:60),
  cohort1 = rnorm(60),
  cohort2 = rnorm(60)
)
df$cohort2 <- 0.65 * df$cohort1 + rnorm(60, 0, 0.5)
plot_concordance(df, "cohort1", "cohort2", title = "Cohort Replication")
